overview.text: The named Blachernae icon is a Hodegetria tradition connected with Constantinople and its later reception in Russia. It must be distinguished from the broad use of Blachernitissa for other Marian compositions.

blocks.text: The OCA recounts an earlier transfer from Jerusalem to Constantinople and associates the icon with the city’s deliverance during siege. It later follows the image through Athos to Moscow, giving 1654 for its gift to Tsar Aleksei Mikhailovich. These are the source’s traditional historical claims.

blocks.text: The earlier Constantinopolitan episode names the empresses Eudokia and Pulcheria and the church where the revered robe of the Mother of God was preserved.

blocks.text: The same page calls the icon Hodegetria, She Who Leads the Way, and connects its memory with praise of the Mother of God. Its heading prints July 7; the narrative also names July 2 and the Saturday of the Akathist. The movable observance is not reduced to a fixed civil date.
